ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) designated list. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is required for all politically exposed persons (PEPs) – foreign, domestic, and international organization PEPs – including their family members and close associates. Screening must be conducted at onboarding, on a continuous basis (at least daily), and upon any trigger event. The AML/CFT compliance program must include risk-based customer due diligence (CDD) measures, transaction monitoring, and suspicious transaction reporting (STR) to KoFIU within 24 hours of detection. For this medium-risk industry (international student placement and immigration visa advisory), additional verification of source of funds and source of wealth is mandatory for all transactions exceeding KRW 10 million (approx. USD 7,500).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea – Internet Registration Office (IRO) – Company Name Search (법인명 검색)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be in Korean (Hangul) script. For foreign entities, a phonetic transliteration into Hangul is required. The name must consist of a distinctive element, a business purpose descriptor, and the legal form suffix (e.g., '유한회사' for LLC). The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered name. The four-tier naming convention includes: (1) distinctive name, (2) business purpose, (3) legal form, and (4) optional trade name. English names may be used as a secondary trade name but must be transliterated into Hangul for registration.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 10000, as subsequently amended), particularly Articles 287-2 through 287-45 governing Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company), Article 289 on the articles of incorporation, and the Korean Commercial Registration Rules under the Court Organization Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the competent Korean District Court under the Supreme Court of Korea, accessed through the Korean Commercial Registration System (IROS) at www.iros.go.kr.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Jeonggwan) together with the Incorporation Registration Application (Seongnip Deunggi Sinaek).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed for a Yuhan Hoesa under Korean law. The members may fix the capital at any amount in the Articles of Incorporation. No blocked escrow account is statutorily required, but contributed funds must be deposited into a domestic capital subscription account in the Company's name and held there until the court registration is completed, after which funds may be used for business operations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF YUHAN HOESA

I, the undersigned Representative Director of Yuhan Hoesa (the Company), acting pursuant to Articles 287-3, 287-4, and 287-8 of the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea and the Company's Articles of Incorporation, hereby adopt the following resolutions:

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: RESOLVED, that the Company subscribes to and issues the number of ordinary shares equal to the member capital contribution recorded in the Articles of Incorporation, and that each member has subscribed to pay the amount allocated opposite their name in the contribution schedule. The Representative Director is directed to collect all contribution proceeds and deposit them in the Company's capital subscription account with a licensed Korean commercial bank, and to obtain the statutory 'Certificate of Subscription Payment' required for registration.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED, that the Representative Director is hereby authorized to open one or more domestic demand deposit, corporate transaction, and escrow accounts in the Company's name; to execute account agreements; to designate the authorized signatories; to wire transfer funds; and to maintain an online banking mandate. Any disbursement exceeding USD 10,000 shall require dual approval by the Representative Director and another designated officer.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: RESOLVED, that the registered office address of the Company shall be [insert full address in Korea], which address is within the jurisdictional district of [insert District Court], and that the Representative Director is authorized to execute the office lease agreement, register the office with the Court Registry, install a corporate signboard, and notify the National Tax Service.

4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer, that [Name] is appointed Internal Director, and that [Name] is appointed Statutory Auditor if required under the Articles or the Commercial Act. Each appointee has consented in writing. The Representative Director shall carry out all incorporation filings and produce certified copies to third parties.

5. ADMINISTRATIVE DELEGATION: RESOLVED, that the Representative Director and any authorized legal agents shall be authorized to sign all applications, powers of attorney, and documents necessary for the registration of incorporation and business license, and to make such corrections as the Registry may require.

This resolution is effective upon adoption and remains in force unless amended by a subsequent board resolution.

Dated this ____ day of _____________ 20____.

[Signature]
[Name and Title]

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Conduct Corporate Name Reservation and Check Entity Formation Eligibility
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the competent Korean District Court through the IROS online portal (www.iros.go.kr)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a corporate name reservation application to the IROS portal of the Supreme Court Registry. Verify that the proposed Yuhan Hoesa name does not conflict with any existing registered trademark or corporate name, and that the name contains a clearly corporate suffix such as 'Yuhan Hoesa' or 'LLC'. The application must include the identity documents of the prospective members or a specific purpose clause. The registry will issue a name reservation certificate with a six-month validity and confirm no identical names are registered. In preparing the application, counsel should also confirm that the intended business of study-abroad and immigration visa advisory services can be lawfully carried out by a Yuhan Hoesa and does not require prior permission from a specific supervisory authority.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form prepared using the IROS-approved template
Passport or alien registration card of each founding member
Power of attorney designating local legal counsel
List of three alternative name choices
Statement of the registered business purpose
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the reserved name is rejected or suspended because of similarity, the applicant may instantly file a new name reservation with alternative names or register an objection administratively through the Supreme Court; however, the most efficient remedy is to submit distinct secondary names. If the registry requests clarification, respond through the IROS portal within seven days attaching corrected articles or a notarized explanation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and Notarize Articles of Incorporation and Consent of Statutory Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Korean Notary Public under Article 55 of the Korean Notary Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation in the Korean language, specifying the corporate purpose, registered office address, capital contribution amount, method of contribution, number of directors, term of the company, and appointment of the initial Representative Director. Each founding member must execute the Articles in person or by proxy with a valid and notarized power of attorney. The notary will verify the identity of signatories and legal registration eligibility, certify the document as a notarial deed, and issue a certified copy. For regulatory compliance, the officers must sign written consents to act, which should be appended. The entire document package should then be lodged with the registry. The notary will determine the final statutory form.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Name reservation certificate
Valid passports or national IDs of all members
Power of attorney if any proxy is used
Written consent forms of proposed Representative Director, any Director, and Statutory Auditor if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses to certify due to insufficient capital description or purpose clause, obtain legal counsel and amend the Articles accordingly. If immigration or visa-consulting activities require any statutory permission, obtain confirmation from the relevant ministry before re-submission; re-execute the Articles and re-notarize without prejudice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit Subscription Capital and Obtain Bank Certificate of Payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean commercial bank branch authorized to accept corporate subscription deposits
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital subscription account in the corporate name with a licensed Korean bank, providing the notarized Articles, name reservation certificate, and identity documents of the registered representative. Deposit the full capital amount specified in the Articles of Incorporation into the account, using the account holder's name and purpose line exactly matching the corporate name. Upon verification of receipt, the bank shall issue a certificate of subscription price payment (Jugeum Napeum Jeungmyeongseo). The certificate is indispensable evidence of contribution and must be appended to the court registration application. Funds may not be disbursed until the court registration certificate is issued.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Name reservation certificate
Passport or alien registration of the representative
Bank account opening application in the corporate name
Certificate of subscription capital payment issued by the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank withholds the certificate because of KYC or anti-money-laundering due diligence, remedy by submitting an updated ultimate beneficial owner declaration and source-of-funds evidence. If funds are transferred from a foreign jurisdiction, provide a wire transfer receipt and a foreign exchange permit or declaration, then re-request certification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Registration with the District Court Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the competent Korean District Court, including the Seoul Central District Court Registry, via IROS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the formal Incorporation Registration Application through the IROS electronic registration system, paying the registration duty and local education surcharge. The filing must include the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the bank issuance of subscription deposit certificate, the name reservation certificate, statutory officer consents, copy of the representative's identification, and a power of attorney executed by the representative. The court registrar verifies identity and accuracy of all corporate details, examines compliance with statutory formalities, and decides to record the entity in the commercial register. Registration issuance is evidenced by a commercial registration certificate containing the corporate registration number. Upon receipt, counsel should confirm the entity number and obtain a certified corporate seal certificate.
required_dossiers: Application for commercial registration
Certified notarial copy of the Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of subscription capital deposit
Name reservation certificate
Consent and appointment forms of statutory officers
Registration duty payment receipt
Power of attorney of legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a supplementary document request, cure by submitting the missing documents through IROS within the usual 14-day grace period. If the application is suspended, resubmit or file an administrative appeal to the Deputy Director of the Registration Office; if necessary, seek a correction order from the competent court. In the event of rejection for a legal deficiency, revise the Articles and re-file a new application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Business with the National Tax Service and File All Post-Incorporation Notices
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) branch with jurisdiction over the registered office and the Hometax online portal (www.hometax.go.kr)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the commercial registration certificate, apply for a business registration certificate with the nearest NTS office or through the Hometax system. Attach evidence of rented office premises, the commercial registration certificate, corporate seal certificate, representative identity, and bank account details. The NTS will issue a certificate assigning a corporate tax number and will automatically enrol the entity for VAT, corporate income tax, and withholding tax obligations. For the advisory activity related to study-abroad and immigration visas, no industrial operating permit is required, but if the company engages in border-crossing placement arrangements, counsel should provide a legal opinion under the Korea Immigration Service and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. Any local municipal business license must be filed within 30 days.
required_dossiers: Commercial registration certificate
Lease agreement for the registered office
Corporate seal certificate
Representative's identification document
Business registration application form
Bank account certificate and banking authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If NTS flags discrepancies in the registered address, submit the corrected lease and address proof within 10 days. If approval is deferred due to a missing license, provide a written explanation of the business scope and obtain any required education or immigration authorization before resubmitting; appeal to the local NTS office director if the assessment is erroneous.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - the entity is a pure consultancy and visa-advisory service carrying on ISIC 7810 activities; there is no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, warehouse or logistics facility.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no industrial operating permit is required. Only the corporate business registration certificate from the National Tax Service is required, as described in SOP Step 5.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Environmental Registration is not required for study-abroad and immigration visa consulting under Korean environmental impact assessment legislation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the business generates no wastewater discharge, no volatile organic compound emissions, no hazardous waste, and no pollutant emission points attributable to the entity's business model.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - the activity generates no fire safety, structural load, or occupational safety approval requirement beyond general office premises compliance. If the company later leases a dedicated office, a standard fire prevention and workplace safety certificate from the local fire department may be required for premises exceeding 146 square metres or under municipal ordinances.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online portal: HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr) for registration, VAT returns, and e-Tax Invoices; Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS (www.unipass.customs.go.kr) for export declarations and export documentation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Korean Yuhan Hoesa (domestic corporation) with foreign shareholders, the tax identity is the 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN) issued by NTS. Procedure: (1) complete Korean Commercial Registry incorporation and obtain the certificate of incorporation; (2) open a corporate bank account and report any non-resident equity investment to a designated foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; (3) within 20 days of business commencement, file a Business Registration Application with the competent NTS district tax office, attaching the articles of incorporation, certificate of incorporation, domestic lease agreement, identification of the domestic representative and foreign shareholders, and the foreign investment remittance certificate; (4) NTS issues the BRN, which functions as the corporate tax TIN and VAT registration number simultaneously; (5) if a foreign non-resident entity has no Korean place of business but supplies or repays VAT-connected Korean-source services, it must separately file a Non-Resident Business Registration through HomeTax, appoint a domestic tax representative for tax collection and refund purposes, and obtain a separate BRN; (6) the same BRN must be referenced on e-Tax Invoices, VAT returns, corporate tax returns, and customs declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. There is no check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election in Korea. A Yuhan Hoesa is automatically an entity-level taxpayer subject to Korean corporate tax on worldwide income. A qualifying wholly-owned Korean domestic subsidiary may elect group consolidated taxation under the Corporate Tax Act; the simplified VAT regime based on the KRW 80,000,000 annual turnover threshold is available only to individual entrepreneurs and not to a corporation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general VAT registration threshold. Any person, including a non-resident foreign entity, making taxable supplies of goods or services in Korea must register as a VAT entrepreneur within 20 days of commencing business. A simplified taxable threshold of KRW 80,000,000 annual turnover is available only to individual small businesses and is not available to a Yuhan Hoesa corporation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Every VAT taxpayer must issue a Korean electronic tax invoice (e-Tax Invoice) for taxable B2B supplies and transmit it operationally to the NTS through HomeTax no later than one day after the supply date. B2C cash transactions of KRW 10,000 or more in cash-receipt-mandatory businesses also require real-time cash receipt transmission. Korea does not operate a physical fiscal stamp or real-time clearance device regime; anti-fraud control is achieved through NTS pre-validation of the Business Registration Number on every e-Tax Invoice, mandatory electronic archive retention, and cross-matching of e-Tax Invoices, credit card data, cash receipts, customs declarations, and foreign exchange receipts. Approved ERP vendors and e-invoice service providers transmit through HomeTax EDI/API interfaces.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Value-Added Tax Act, exported goods are zero-rated once the export declaration is accepted by Korea Customs Service and the goods depart Korea. Export services are zero-rated only if expressly recognized as exported services under the VAT Act and Presidential Decree. For study-abroad placement and immigration visa consulting, zero-rating applies when the Yuhan Hoesa supplies the service to a non-resident counterparty, the service is performed and consumed outside Korea, and consideration is received in foreign currency. Commission income from offshore schools, overseas immigration authorities, or non-resident principals can qualify. Fees charged to Korean resident students or to applicants for Korean visas are taxable at 10%. Qualifying digital services that are delivered offshore to non-residents and paid in foreign currency may also be zero-rated. Excess input VAT attributable to zero-rated exports is refundable under the VAT Act.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: For goods: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration Certificate issued through UNI-PASS, bill of lading or air waybill, commercial invoice, packing list, and a foreign exchange bank certificate proving receipt of foreign currency export proceeds.

For zero-rated study-abroad and immigration advisory services: written contract with the non-resident counterparty, commercial invoice denominated in foreign currency, foreign currency receipt certificate issued by a designated Korean foreign exchange bank, service delivery documentation such as admission letters, visa approvals, placement confirmations or service completion reports, and a signed client statement confirming the service was performed and consumed offshore.

Where the Yuhan Hoesa acts as an intermediary for overseas schools or immigration authorities, retain the agency agreement, the principal's invoice, and the onward foreign currency remittance evidence to substantiate the offshore supply.

Digital service exports: retain the user subscription or service contract, server or delivery location evidence confirming overseas use, payment gateway records, foreign currency receipts, and a technical delivery report where applicable.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is heavily audited by NTS. If the complete substantiation bundle is not preserved, or the export consideration is not received in foreign currency within the statutory 180-day period without an approved extension from a designated foreign exchange bank, the zero-rate is retroactively clawed back and the supply is reclassified as a domestic taxable supply. NTS will then assess VAT at 10%, together with statutory additional taxes for under-reporting and late payment under the Framework Act on National Taxes, and, in cases of fabricated export documentation or false e-Tax Invoices, criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, including imprisonment or fines of up to several times the evaded tax, and a discretionary 40% fraud penalty. Failure to repatriate proceeds may also trigger penalties under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, including administrative fines, export restriction orders, and compliance sanctions. NTS continuously cross-matches export declarations, e-Tax Invoices, corporate bank accounts, and foreign exchange receipts to identify overclaimed zero-rated supplies.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea, operating in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the Korea Federation of Banks' Foreign Exchange Information System under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic of Korea maintains a liberalized foreign exchange market with statutory reporting obligations rather than blanket surrender requirements. The won is convertible for current account transactions, including fees for study-abroad placement and immigration visa services, subject to documentary evidence and settlement through authorized foreign exchange banks. Capital account transactions, including inbound direct investment in a Yuhan Hoesa, require declaration and registration under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, but there is no fixed lower-layer notification threshold for equity subscribed by foreign investors. Profit remittances are permitted once corporate taxes, withholding taxes, and external audits are satisfied; the branch/company must present audited financial statements and a tax clearance certificate in order to remit dividends abroad. Foreign currency proceeds may be retained in designated foreign currency deposit accounts, and there is no statutory mandate to convert export or service receipts into won at a fixed ratio. However, any conversion into KRW must be executed with a licensed foreign exchange bank at market rates, and all cross-border settlement events must be transmitted to the Korea Federation of Banks for statistical and AML surveillance. In practice, the greatest hurdles are documentary: a Korean bank will require full underlying contracts, capital verification certificates, and an explanatory memorandum for each significant inbound wire before treating the funds as cleared operating capital. The absence of minimum paid-in capital does not exempt the entity from enhanced due diligence, and perceived mismatches between the corporate purpose, remitter profile, and client geography will attract further scrutiny. Overall, the Korean FX regime is best characterized as regulatory liberalization with intensive ex post reporting rather than hard administrative rationing of foreign exchange.

stage_4.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export and service proceeds from international student placement and immigration visa advisory engagements must be collected within 90 calendar days from the date of the related export/service declaration or contract milestone, unless the foreign exchange bank approves a longer collection period. The statutory surrender ratio to the Bank of Korea is 0%: there is no requirement to convert foreign currency export receipts into KRW, and companies may retain the funds in foreign currency deposit accounts at authorized foreign exchange banks. If the Yuhan Hoesa chooses to convert receipts into KRW, the conversion must be performed through a licensed foreign exchange bank at the commercial exchange rate. Any failure to collect export/service proceeds within the 90-day timeline requires a corrective report to the responsible foreign exchange bank and may trigger an administrative investigation for FIU reporting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 of the year immediately following the fiscal year-end (December 31); if the due date falls on a non-business day, the next business day.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing triggers additional tax of 40% of the tax amount (20% for underreporting), delinquency interest of 0.022% per day, tax liens and asset seizure; three consecutive years of non-operation and non-filing may trigger court-initiated administrative strike-off or dissolution under Commercial Act Article 520bis.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Surtax Return and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Si/Gun/Gu local government tax authority via Wetax local tax filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 of the year following the fiscal year-end, matching the national corporate income tax filing deadline.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Local surtax penalties mirror the national corporate tax penalties: 40% additional tax for non-filing, 20% for underreporting, 0.022% daily delinquency interest, seizure of assets, and denial of tax clearance certificates needed for license renewal.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Return (First Half Preliminary Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: July 25 of the same calendar year for the January 1 - June 30 VAT filing period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or underpayment triggers VAT additional tax plus 0.022% daily delinquency interest; repeated non-filing may result in business registration cancellation and compulsory tax collection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Return (Second Half Final Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 25 of the following calendar year for the July 1 - December 31 VAT filing period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or underpayment triggers VAT additional tax plus 0.022% daily delinquency interest; persistent failure permits forced closure of the place of business and asset seizure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Municipal Per-Capita Equalization Resident Tax for Corporations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Assessed as of July 1 and payable on or before July 31 of each calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delinquency accrues 0.022% daily local-tax interest; unpaid equalization tax leads to seizure of bank accounts and refusal of tax clearance certificates, blocking regulatory license renewal and immigration-program approvals.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Auditor's Report and Audited Financial Statements (only if compulsory audit threshold is met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) designated electronic disclosure system plus the National Tax Service; copy retained at the registered office for member inspection.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two weeks after the annual members' meeting, which must be held by March 31 of the following fiscal year; in no event later than April 30 for a December 31 fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an independent auditor or submit the report can trigger administrative fines under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies of up to KRW 100 million, refusal to accept the corporate income tax return, enhanced tax investigation, and disqualification from regulatory licensing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-Invested Enterprise Annual Status Report (if foreign shareholding exists)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through KOTRA and the managing foreign-exchange bank
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the fiscal year-end, i.e., on or before March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year; any change in UBO, shareholding, or capital must additionally be reported within 30 days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of up to KRW 5 million for late or false filing; possible loss of foreign-investment tax incentives, restricted dividend repatriation, and adverse treatment for escrow and golden-visa program approvals.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Members' Meeting Resolution and Statutory Register Review Certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate record maintained at the registered office; court registration may be triggered if the resolution changes directors or the registered office.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual members' meeting must be convened within three months of the fiscal year-end, i.e., by March 31 for a December 31 year-end; director and registered-office changes must be registered with the local court registry within two weeks of the resolution.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the annual meeting or update statutory register data may render resolutions void, incur administrative enforcement fines, and constitute grounds for a court order to remove directors or dissolve the company.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent certified audit is required for the Yuhan Hoesa LLC if any of the following thresholds is met under the Korean Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, its Enforcement Decree, or the applicable license conditions: (i) total assets at the immediately preceding fiscal year-end equal or exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 8.9 million); (ii) total annual operating turnover from study-abroad placement, immigration advisory, and visa services equals or exceeds KRW 20 billion and the year-end headcount is 100 or more full-time employees; (iii) the company is a member of a group required to prepare consolidated financial statements and the group's combined assets equal or exceed KRW 12 billion; (iv) members holding at least 20% of the equity interests lawfully demand an external audit under Article 4 of the External Audit Act; (v) the company holds, receives, or disburses escrow deposits from study-abroad or immigration clients in aggregate exceeding KRW 5 billion in a fiscal year, because licensed non-bank escrow advisory activities impose a certified-accounting safeguard; or (vi) any license condition imposed by the Ministry of Justice, Ministry of Education, or immigration-licensing authority requires audited financial statements for the relevant visa-advisory or student-placement operation. The engagement must be executed by an independent certified public accountant registered with the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants (KICPA).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared under Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for companies subject to mandatory external audit; non-listed small limited companies not meeting the audit thresholds may apply Korean GAAP or the Korean SME Accounting Standards (SME Standards) for small and medium-sized entities. In all cases, corporate income tax book-adjustment schedules reconciling statutory accounting income with taxable income under the Corporate Income Tax Act must be prepared for the annual corporate income tax return. Commercial Act record-keeping rules require preservation of commercial books and related material records for ten years.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Yuhan Hoesa must maintain a current register of ultimate beneficial owners at its Korean registered office and reconfirm the ownership schedule at the annual members' meeting no later than March 31 following the December 31 fiscal year-end. Any share transfer, issuance, pledge, or direct or indirect change in beneficial ownership must be reported to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) and, for foreign investors, to the managing foreign-exchange bank within 30 days of the change; the same 30-day window applies to the annual confirmation filing with the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy. The register must identify every UBO being an individual who owns or controls at least 25% of the equity or voting rights or who exercises control through other means, including the UBO's full legal name, nationality, tax residence, and proportionate economic interest. If no such individual is identified, the senior resident director must be named as the controlling person in the compliance register.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national corporate income tax marginal rate; aggregate 26.4% when the 10% local income tax surcharge is included
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No patent-box or general free-zone preferential rate applies to ISIC 7810 study-abroad/immigration visa consulting; general incentives under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act include R&D tax credits, employment tax credits, and, for a qualified Foreign-Invested Enterprise physically located in an Incheon or Free Economic Zone, a 100% corporate income tax exemption for 3 years and a 50% reduction for the next 2 years; the consulting fee income of the Yuhan Hoesa is otherwise taxed at the normal progressive rates.
